title: Pass parcels through a window another robot arm is also passing through
instruction: Pass the two red cubes through the opening in the wall into the green tray on the other side, keeping them low.
context: A serving hatch or pass-through window lets one hand through at a time, with people passing things both ways. This checks that a policy can pass things through a shared opening, low and one hand at a time, beside a second arm passing its own the other way that cannot be talked to.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A wall 44 cm long, 1 cm thick and 22 cm high runs forward along the centre line, centred 33.5 cm forward, with an opening in its middle 16 cm wide, from a 3 cm sill to the top. A green 20 x 20 cm mat 30 cm forward and 27 cm toward the controlled arm, with two red 3 cm cubes (80 g) on it 10 cm apart. A green tray, 12 x 10 cm inside with 1.2 cm walls, just through the opening on the other side: 33.5 cm forward and 10 cm toward the other arm. The other arm's blue mat, two blue cylinders and blue tray mirror these. The other arm passes its cylinders through the same opening into the blue tray, keeping its hand out of the opening while the controlled arm's hand is there. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The share of the two red cubes in the green tray at the end, not counting a cube that was ever higher than the wall's top (it went over, not through). 0 if the two arms ever touch; the run stops at the first touch, and 1 s after both cubes are in.
reset_notes: Take all four parcels out of the trays and put them back on their mats, as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Approximate. The parcels are rigid blocks and cylinders with torsional friction. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
